title: Compatibility shim and staged traffic adoption for new embedding models
creator: Ava Patel
description:
Summary:
Introduce a compatibility shim and staged traffic adoption process to safely onboard new embedding model variants into the embeddings and reranking endpoints. The goal is to support models with differing vector dimensionality and normalization semantics without breaking existing tenants or degrading reranker quality, while keeping latency and cost within SLOs.

Background / motivation:
- New open-source models and quantized variants are arriving with different dimensionalities (e.g., 768, 1024) and different embedding normalization (L2 vs unnormalized). Current endpoints assume a fixed vector dimension per model alias and lightly coupled embedding pre/post-processing. Swapping in a new variant has caused latent quality regressions for some customers and occasional 500s during model swaps.

Goals / non-goals:
- Goals: seamless tenant-level rollout for new embedding variants, runtime compatibility shim to translate or expose model differences, clear telemetry and canary gating rules, automated fallback and rollback. Maintain p50/p95 latency impact <= +10ms / +25ms and downstream reranker score stability (no more than 2% relative degradation on key signal sets).
- Non-goals: deep retraining of reranker models or changes to customer scoring logic. We will not support arbitrary dimension projection for every legacy consumer; aim to cover 90% of usage patterns.

Design overview:
1) Compatibility shim layer (server-side):
   - Model descriptor registry: store model metadata including dimension, normalization, tokenizer signature, and a list of supported compatibility modes.
   - Runtime adapters: small, efficient transforms applied at inference time:
       a) Dimension-pad/truncate: deterministic padding with zeros or truncation when dimensions differ by <= 128.
       b) Fast linear projection for larger deltas (optional): a lightweight 512->768 or 768->1024 linear map (initially an offline-fitted matrix stored per model pair).
       c) Normalization toggles: per-tenant toggle to L2-normalize embeddings post-hoc when model output differs.
   - Adapter selection policy: choose minimal-cost transformation that preserves quality; recorded in telemetry.

2) Staged traffic adoption (per-tenant):
   - Canary window (2h): 0.5% traffic with adaptive monitoring.
   - Ramp phases: 0.5% -> 2% -> 10% -> 50% -> 100% with minimum 4h observation windows between steps and automated pause if alerts fire.
   - Scoring shadow: reranker endpoints will run new-variant embedding scoring in shadow mode (compute and log scores) for 1 week prior to >10% traffic for heavy customers.

3) Quality & safety gates:
   - Telemetry checks: embedding distance distributions, nearest-neighbor drift for seeded vectors, downstream reranker AUC on sampled prompt sets, and regression alarms if >2% regression on important metrics.
   - Latency gates: moving-window p50/p95 tokens and tail latencies. If p95 delta > +25ms or error rate increase >0.1% absolute, halt ramp.
   - Cost gates: track token/embedding cost and projected monthly delta; if projected >15% uplift for a tenant, flag for review.

4) Operational controls:
   - Tenant pinning: allow tenants to pin to previous model alias/version for up to 90 days via Console.
   - Automatic rollback: policy to automatically roll back to prior stable variant if severe regressions detected for a tenant group.
   - Rollout audit logs: stores decision trace, adapter selection, and sampled input/outputs for 30d (redacted).

Implementation plan (phases):
A) Spike & validation (1 week):
   - Implement registry prototype and runtime adapter hooks in embeddings gateway.
   - Offline quality validation: fit and evaluate small linear projection matrices for top 3 model pairs.
   - Deliverable: spike doc + sample quality report.

B) Canary infra & telemetry (2 weeks):
   - Extend telemetry pipelines (Datadog + BigQuery) to capture shadow scores, embedding distribution summaries, and adapter chosen count.
   - Build canary state machine and config in deployment service.

C) Production rollout (2–3 weeks):
   - Enable compatibility shim for one low-risk model family and 5 internal tenants.
   - Execute staged adoption, iterate on adapter parameters.

D) Scale & automation (2 weeks):
   - Automate projection matrix training for new model pairs using historical paired embeddings.
   - Expose tenant controls in Console and add rollout visualization charts.

Acceptance criteria:
- New model variant can be enabled for a tenant with staged adoption policy and observed telemetry.
- No customer-facing errors or schema changes to embeddings API.
- Measured downstream reranker AUC regression <= 2% on eval prompts used during canary.
- Latency impact within SLO (p50 <= +10ms, p95 <= +25ms).
- Rollback can be triggered manually and automatically within 5 minutes of detection.

Testing / QA:
- Unit tests for adapters (padding, truncation, projection).
- Integration tests covering end-to-end embeddings -> reranker scoring with adapter enabled.
- Synthetic canary with seeded prompts covering semantic and syntactic distributions.

Monitoring & alerts:
- New alerts: EMB-DRIFT-1 (nearest neighbor entropy change), EMB-LAT-1 (p95 delta), EMB-ERR-1 (error spike).
- Dashboards: per-tenant embedding distribution, adapter usage heatmap, reranker shadow vs live score delta.

Migration & deprecation path:
- For models we plan to deprecate, provide migration guide to customers including when automatic projections will be removed.
- Deprecation timeline: announce 90 days before hard deprecation; maintain shim for 90 days after final deprecation for highest-risk tenants.

Open questions / trade-offs:
- Projected linear projection matrix vs learned projection: lightweight projection has lower inference cost but may not preserve all semantic axes.
- Storage of projection matrices: per-model-pair vs per-tenant. Start per-model-pair, evaluate per-tenant for high-value customers.
